items.title: Discord voice receive path ignores RTP padding before DAVE/Opus decode
items.body:
## Summary

The Discord voice receive path appears to ignore the RTP padding bit on inbound audio packets before handing payload bytes to DAVE decrypt / Opus decode.

In practice, this can make Discord voice channels appear deaf or intermittently return empty STT results, especially on the first real user reply after join.

## Why this looks like a real protocol bug

During live packet capture and offline analysis of a failing Discord VC session:

- all offline decode failures came from RTP packets whose first byte was `0xb0`
- `0xb0` means:
  - RTP version 2
  - padding bit = 1
  - extension bit = 1
  - CSRC count = 0
- no unpadded packet in the same trace failed offline decode
- several failing payloads became structurally plausible once the repeated trailing bytes indicated by the final byte count were removed
- some trimmed payloads ended in `...0d fafa`, which strongly suggests DAVE framing was still present and we were passing padding-contaminated payloads deeper into the stack

Per RFC 3550, when RTP padding is set, the last payload byte is the padding count and those trailing bytes are not part of the media payload.

So the expected inbound order is:

1. RTP header parse
2. outer transport decrypt
3. strip encrypted RTP header-extension bytes
4. strip RTP padding bytes if the padding bit is set
5. DAVE inner media decrypt
6. Opus decode

The current receive path appears to do 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and skip step 4.

## Additional protocol note

While investigating this, exact `0xF8FFFE` payloads showed up in the trace. Those are legitimate Opus silence packets, not corruption:

- Discord voice docs describe `0xF8, 0xFF, 0xFE` as the silence/interpolation packet
- Discord `libdave` explicitly preserves exact `0xF8FFFE` and skips decrypting it

So the issue is not that silence packets are bad; it is that padded packets are reaching DAVE / Opus without the RTP padding bytes being removed first.

## Impact observed

Symptoms on live Discord VC sessions included:

- first user reply after join sometimes appearing lost
- repeated `corrupted stream` decode behavior on inbound receive
- turns that reached STT but came back empty despite audible user speech
- greeting / farewell playback working while inbound speech looked broken

After stripping RTP padding before DAVE / Opus in a downstream branch, inbound speech started working reliably from the first real reply in the same environment.

## Suggested fix

Handle RTP padding on inbound Discord UDP audio packets after transport decrypt and extension stripping, but before DAVE media decrypt / Opus decode.

Pseudocode shape:

```python
has_padding = bool(first_byte & 0x20)
...
decrypted = transport_decrypt(...)
if ext_data_len:
    decrypted = decrypted[ext_data_len:]
if has_padding and decrypted:
    pad_len = decrypted[-1]
    if 0 < pad_len <= len(decrypted):
        decrypted = decrypted[:-pad_len]
    else:
        drop packet / log invalid padding
# then continue with DAVE decrypt / Opus decode
```

## Reference points

- RFC 3550 RTP padding semantics
- Discord voice docs on silence packets
- `discord/libdave` preserving exact `0xF8FFFE`

If helpful, I can open a follow-up PR with the padding fix isolated from any other local Discord voice changes.

items.title: fix(delegate): treat toolsets=[] as explicit empty toolset, not inheritance

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Bug Description

On `origin/main`, `delegate_task(toolsets=[])` is treated as falsy inside `_build_child_agent()`, so an explicit empty list is interpreted as “no toolsets argument was provided”.

As a result, the child agent inherits the parent toolsets instead of receiving zero tools.

## Root Cause

In `tools/delegate_tool.py` on `origin/main`, the toolset-selection branch uses:

```python
if toolsets:
```

That conflates two different cases:

- `toolsets is None` → omitted; inherit parent/default behavior
- `toolsets == []` → explicit empty set; child should get no tools

Because `[]` is falsy, the explicit-empty case falls through to the inheritance branch.

## Why This Matters

This breaks workflows that intentionally spawn review-only or reasoning-only subagents with no tools. For example, `adversary-review` recommends `toolsets: []` so the reviewer cannot go off and perform extra research.

With the current behavior on `origin/main`, the child can unexpectedly inherit `web`, `browser`, or other parent toolsets and do work it was supposed to be unable to do.

## Reproduction

1. Create a parent agent with `enabled_toolsets=["terminal", "file", "web"]`
2. On `origin/main`, call `_build_child_agent(..., toolsets=[], parent_agent=parent)`
3. Inspect the child `enabled_toolsets`
4. Actual: `['terminal', 'file', 'web']`
5. Expected: `[]`

## Expected Behavior

- `toolsets=None` should preserve the existing inheritance behavior
- `toolsets=[]` should produce a child with no enabled toolsets

## Proposed Fix

Change the branch condition to distinguish omission from explicit empty input:

```python
if toolsets is not None:
```

and add a regression test covering `toolsets=[]`.

## Regression Test

A targeted regression test can assert that:

- `toolsets=[]` yields `enabled_toolsets == []`
- `toolsets=None` still inherits as before

items.title: QQbot cannot process images: url_safety blocks Tencent CDN domain due to local proxy IP flagged as private
items.body:
## Description

When sending an image to the QQbot, the request is blocked by url_safety with the following warning:

```
WARNING tools.url_safety: Blocked request to private/internal address: multimedia.nt.qq.com.cn -> 198.18.1.83
```

As a result, `images=0` and the image is never downloaded or processed.

## Important correction

The IP `198.18.1.83` is **not** the actual resolved IP of Tencent's CDN. It is the address of the user's local proxy virtual interface (utun). The domain `multimedia.nt.qq.com.cn` goes through a local proxy, causing it to resolve to this interface address.

The url_safety module performs DNS resolution on the domain and checks if the resulting IP is private/reserved. Python's `ipaddress` marks the `198.18.0.0/15` range (RFC 2544 benchmark) as private, leading to false positives for legitimate CDN domains when a local proxy is used.

## Expected behavior

Requests to `multimedia.nt.qq.com.cn` should be allowed regardless of the resolved IP, as it is a legitimate Tencent CDN domain.

## Proposed fix

Add a whitelist for Tencent QQ CDN domains in `tools/url_safety.py` to skip the private address check. For example:

```python
ALLOWED_DOMAINS = {"multimedia.nt.qq.com.cn"}
```

Or more broadly, skip the private IP check for domains that are known CDNs.

## Environment

- macOS with local proxy (utun interface)
- Hermes Agent latest main branch

## Log excerpt

```
2026-04-16 23:35:51,667 INFO gateway.platforms.qqbot: [QQ] attachment[0]: content_type=image/jpeg url=https://multimedia.nt.qq.com.cn/...
2026-04-16 23:35:51,676 WARNING tools.url_safety: Blocked request to private/internal address: multimedia.nt.qq.com.cn -> 198.18.1.83
```
